claims.claim: The query is a 1-cyclopropyl-6-fluoro-8-methoxy-4-oxo-3-carboxylic acid fluoroquinolone; reference fluoroquinolones with this core have measured human absolute oral bioavailability of 87.6–100% (trovafloxacin, levofloxacin, ofloxacin), and antofloxacin shows an oral/IV AUC ratio of about 1.1.

L5 gut-wall efflux records show that fluoroquinolones can be P-gp/BCRP/MRP2 substrates and that transporter inhibition can increase oral AUC (enrofloxacin, ciprofloxacin, gemifloxacin, grepafloxacin, danofloxacin), but these are mechanistic observations, not direct F measurements, and the same chemotype still reaches F well above 20%.

Some L5 records support adequate absorption or minimal net efflux: moxifloxacin efflux ratios fell to 1.20–1.25 with MRP2/MDR1 inhibitors and ciprofloxacin showed a rat jejunum Papp of 5.1 × 10^-6 cm/s.

No L5 record provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20%; the uncertain physicochemical prior (fully ionized, logD -0.47) is not endpoint proof and is outweighed by transferable direct F evidence.

The 7-substituent in the query is a fluoroalkene-containing piperidine with a primary amine, which is not represented in the reference high-F set; its transporter and metabolic behavior are inferred by analogy.
No formulation-, dose-, or species-matched data for the exact query are present.
L5 records are mechanistic efflux observations, not matched oral-versus-IV absolute bioavailability determinations.

The uncertain physicochemical prior does not override the transferable experimental evidence.
